title: POC capacity & routing strategy
content:
Summary:
This is a working decision canvas for the retail-customer POC (customer: BrightCart). Goal: choose an initial deployment architecture and routing/capacity policy that balances latency SLOs, predictable cost, data controls, and ease of rollback during the 6-week POC.

Context and constraints (customer):
- BrightCart is evaluating a conversational product recommender integrated into their storefront and internal agent.
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 250ms for simple prompts; 95th <= 700ms for complex top-k reranking calls.
- Sensitive PII in agent conversations requires optional data residency + audit logs.
- Expected QPS: 10 steady with 3x peak during promotions. Token distribution: short prompts (~40 tokens) for recommendations, long prompts (~600 tokens) for chat context.
- Ops scope: customer wants to avoid full infra ops for POC but needs strong observability and ability to trigger model rollbacks.

Decision criteria (ranked):
1) Meets latency SLOs at 95th under peak load
2) Predictable unit cost and visible cost breakdown
3) Data control / residency + auditability
4) Fast failover & simple rollback (canary/checkpointing)
5) Time-to-first-POC (how fast we can get customer testing)
6) Security posture (VPC/KMS)

Candidate architectures evaluated:
- Hosted-only (Redwood API, multi-tenant): fastest demo velocity; limited residency options; lower ops for customer; can use model variants for fallbacks.
- Dedicated pool + routing via Redwood Console: reserved capacity in a single region, customer traffic routed to dedicated pool; provides predictable throughput and stronger isolation; supports rollouts/canaries.
- Private deployment (VPC-hosted control plane + on-prem or cloud private nodes): full data control and KMS integration; longer setup time; we plan this only if customer signs enterprise contract.

Routing & capacity strategy options (detailed):
A) Cost-first routing (default): route non-sensitive, bursty traffic to hosted; route sensitive or high-cost model variants to dedicated/private. Pros: cheap, simple. Cons: introduces multiple code paths, potential latency variance.

B) Latency-first routing (preferred for this POC): route all low-latency endpoints to dedicated pool sized for sustained QPS + cushion; fallback to hosted only when dedicated exhausted (graceful degrade to cheaper model). Pros: predictable latency, single code path for main flows. Cons: higher committed cost.

C) Hybrid-by-feature: chat->dedicated, embeddings+batch tasks->hosted. Pros: balances cost and SLOs. Cons: requires per-route policy config and testing.

Key engineering patterns to implement during POC:
- Smart fallback chain: primary model on dedicated, fallback model (quantized) on hosted with transparent token/cost accounting.
- Autoscale guardrails: configure dedicated autoscale min to cover steady QPS and max to cap cost; use burst capacity for short promotions.
- Prefix/KV caching for chat to avoid regen of repeated context across retries; measure cache hit-rate early.
- Instrument per-route token and latency metrics; ingest into Console dashboard and add alert for 95th > threshold.

Cost sketch (back-of-envelope):
- Dedicated baseline (small pool) to service 10 QPS steady at short prompt latency target: estimated commit ~$6k/month (GPU/flavor dependent).
- Hosted fallback usage for promotions ~estimated $300-$1,200 per promotion day depending on model mix.
- Engineering effort: ~2 eng weeks to wire canary + routing policies + dashboards.

Observability & failure modes:
- Trace points: client -> routing layer -> pool selection -> model variant. Add span ids for cache hits and fallback triggers.
- Failure mode 1: Dedicated pool OOMs -> fallback to hosted quantized model; user-visible slower responses. Add 5xx rate alert + auto-fallback policy.
- Failure mode 2: Networking partition (customer VPC) -> redirect to hosted non-sensitive path, mark PII flag suppressed and log event for audit.

Security and dataflow notes:
- For Private option, KMS/HSM integration required; otherwise for Dedicated, support bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via KMS link.
- Audit logs need to be forwarded to customer's SIEM via S3/CloudTrail-compatible sink. Add sample log schema to Confluence (linked artifact).

POC test plan (6-week timeline):
Week 0: Kickoff + baseline latency/cost targets. Provision dedicated pool with minimal commit.
Week 1-2: Integrate customer app; validate simple chat path; baseline traces and dashboards.
Week 3: Exercise peak promotion traffic via load tests; adjust autoscale policies.
Week 4: Enable fallback chain and run failover drills (kill dedicated nodes, simulate latency).
Week 5: Data residency verification + audit export test.
Week 6: Collect metrics, customer demo, decision review; recommend next steps (upgrade to private or expand dedicated).

Open questions / risks (to resolve in week 0-1):
- Does BrightCart require all logs to remain in EU? If yes, hosted-only is not viable for primary traffic.
- Approval for short-term commit budget for dedicated pool (estimate: $6k/mo) — who signs?
- Which internal teams at BrightCart will own the failover playbook? Need contacts.

Action items (owner initials):
- Maya: draft canary and rollback playbook + sample routing policy JSON (due 2024-11-08).
- Diego: run RTT/layered-latency tests for dedicated pool and hosted quantized variant (due 2024-11-10).
- Priya: map compliance requirements with customer security team (due 2024-11-07).
- Samir: prepare Console dashboard template and alert rules (due 2024-11-09).

Notes to self / meeting fragments:
- "If they accept small commit, latency-first gives cleaner UX for storefront"
- "Consider moving embeddings to hosted to save commit dollars, but watch for cross-region cost"
- "We need clear UX doc for devs explaining per-route policy — low ceremony to change during POC"

Appendix (quick commands & references):
- sample routing policy snippet: redwood route set --name storefront --primary dedicated:pool-a:gpu-v2 --fallback hosted:quantized-gpt-small --slo 95:250ms
- load test harness: github.com/redwood-inference/poc-scripts#retail-loads
- Confluence primer: CONFLUENCE-12345 (POC onboarding checklist)

End of canvas. This file is a living doc; expect iterative edits after the kickoff meeting.
